title: Federigo's Falcon
text:
Federigo degli Alberighi was a young nobleman of Florence who fell in love with Monna Giovanna, a married lady. To win her he held feasts and tournaments and spent his whole fortune, but she, being virtuous, paid him no attention. Ruined, he retired to a little farm outside the city, where he lived poorly. The only thing of value he had left was a magnificent falcon.

Giovanna's husband died, and she spent the summer at a country house near Federigo's farm with her young son. The boy became friends with Federigo and fell in love with the falcon. Then he fell seriously ill and told his mother that if he could have the falcon, he would get well.

Giovanna went to ask for it, embarrassed. Federigo, overjoyed at her visit, wanted to give her a meal, but there was nothing in the house. Without hesitating, he killed his fine falcon, had it roasted and served it to her. After dinner she made her request. Federigo burst into tears and told her she had just eaten it.

She was sorry for the falcon but moved by his greatness of soul. Her son died a few days later. When her brothers pressed her to remarry, she chose Federigo, saying she would rather have a man who lacked money than money that lacked a man. He married her and from then on managed his wealth wisely.
lesson: Character shows most clearly when someone gives freely with nothing left over. Look for generosity of spirit in people, not only for what they own.
people: Federigo degli Alberighi, Monna Giovanna, her son
